sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Stokes County?
sections.html:
The Stokes County Tax Administration office in the Administration Building at 1014 Main Street, Danbury, handles listing, assessment, billing and collection. Its mailing address is P.O. Box 57, and it keeps hours of 8:30 am to 5:00 pm Monday through Friday.

The department publishes a tax search and payment portal, property record cards, land and home values, an online listing service and a form for extension requests. It also offers e-statements for owners who prefer not to receive paper bills.

sections.h2: When are Stokes County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills must be paid by January 5 to avoid interest, and mailed payments must be postmarked by that date. State law makes taxes payable on September 1, with interest beginning January 6.

  • January 6 through the end of January: 2% interest.
  • From February 1 until paid: three quarters of one percent for each month or part of a month.

For a seller, the practical point is that a bill for the year of sale is a lien on the parcel and has to be settled or credited at closing. Ask Tax Administration for the current balance on your parcel before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: How does a Stokes County owner list property and what is the penalty?
sections.html:
The listing period is January 1 through January 31 each year. The county commissioners may extend it by up to 30 days in a year without a general reappraisal, and individual extensions for good cause can run to April 15 if requested during the listing period.

Stokes County posts a 10% penalty on the total tax levied for failure to list within the period. Real estate owners with no changes rarely need to do anything, but anyone who built, tore down or bought business or personal property should list it.

sections.h2: How often does Stokes County reappraise real property?
sections.html:
Stokes County reappraises on a four-year cycle, which is shorter than the statewide eight-year maximum in G.S. 105-286. The county notes that in years without a general reappraisal, the assessor can change a value only in narrow cases, such as correcting a clerical or mathematical error or fixing a misapplied schedule.

The county's page also says the assessor may adjust value for factors other than normal depreciation, countywide economic conditions or minor improvements like repainting. Ask Tax Administration for the effective date of the current reappraisal on your parcel's notice.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Stokes County value?
sections.html:
Start with a call to the Tax Administration office, then go to the Board of Equalization and Review if you are not satisfied. State law has the board meet first no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May, and a hearing request must reach it before it adjourns.

Appeal steps for a Stokes County real estate value
StepWhere the rule comes from
Informal talk with the assessorTax Administration, Danbury
Hearing before the county boardG.S. 105-322: request before the board adjourns
Appeal to the Property Tax CommissionG.S. 105-290: notice within 30 days after the board mailed its decision

The Stokes County board meeting dates change yearly, so ask Tax Administration for the current schedule.

sections.h2: What tax relief exists for Stokes County homeowners?
sections.html:
The county's FAQ describes the elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of the appraised value of a permanent residence, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, with income not above the limit the page prints as $38,800. The state also runs a disabled veteran exclusion of the first $45,000 of value and a circuit breaker deferment that limits tax to 4% or 5% of income.

  • Applications go to the county assessor, not the state.
  • An owner may use only one of the three programs.
  • The county publishes the application forms on its tax pages.

The income limit is adjusted by the state each year, so confirm the figure for your tax year at the office.

sections.h2: What should a Stokes County seller do about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Get a clear balance and a certification. Stokes County requires that deeds carry a certification from Tax Administration that no delinquent taxes are owed on the property, so an open bill stops the deed at the recorder's counter.

If the tax is behind, remember that unpaid real estate tax is a lien and the county can bring a foreclosure action against the parcel. Paying from sale proceeds is common, and an as-is cash buyer can close around a past-due balance as long as it is cleared at closing.

sections.h2: What happens if Stokes County property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
State law attaches the lien on the date property is listed, with penalties, interest and costs added at the same time. The county can enforce it by an action in the nature of a mortgage foreclosure filed in the county where the land lies, and the owner of record and other lienholders must be served.

  • The sale is a public auction to the highest bidder at the courthouse door.
  • The commissioner may require a deposit of up to 20% of the bid.
  • Exceptions or an increased bid can be filed within 10 days after the sale report.
  • Before confirmation, you can redeem by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

If a bill is behind, call Tax Administration now. A past-due balance is far easier to settle than a foreclosure action.

sections.h2: How does Stokes County value personal property such as mobile equipment or business assets?
sections.html:
Personal property is appraised each year as of January 1 at its true value in money. The county asks owners to list at original cost by year of acquisition, then trends the cost to current replacement cost and applies straight line depreciation, using schedules developed by the state Department of Revenue.

Inventories of manufacturers, retailers, wholesalers and contractors, and non-business personal property, are exempt by statute. Any appraisal can be appealed to the local county board and then to the Property Tax Commission. Stokes County also posts a list of its top ten taxpayers on the FAQ page.

sections.h2: How do the three homestead programs differ for a Stokes County owner?
sections.html:
The elderly or disabled exclusion and the disabled veteran exclusion reduce the taxable value, while the circuit breaker defers part of the bill. The veteran program has no age or income limit, and the unmarried surviving spouse of a qualifying veteran can also apply.

The circuit breaker requires five years of ownership and occupancy as a permanent residence. The state form text prints a limit of $38,800 and $58,200 for the 2026 tax year, and applications are accepted through June 1 before the tax year. The deferred amounts for the preceding three fiscal years become due when the owner transfers the home, dies or stops living there.

sections.h2: Can a Stokes County owner pay in advance or get a discount?
sections.html:
State law lets a county adopt a prepayment discount by resolution, adopted by May 1 before the due date and approved by the Department of Revenue. Stokes County's published FAQ does not describe a discount, so ask Tax Administration whether one applies. Mailed payments count on the postmark date, which matters near January 5.

Owners who sell mid-year should also ask the closing attorney how the year's bill will be split between buyer and seller, since the bill goes to the parcel owner of record.

faqs.q: When are Stokes County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment by January 5 avoids interest, and mailed payments need a postmark of January 5. Interest starts January 6.

faqs.q: What is the Stokes County listing period?
faqs.a: January 1 through January 31, with possible extensions of 30 days from the commissioners or individual extensions up to April 15 for good cause.

faqs.q: Does Stokes County charge a penalty for not listing?
faqs.a: Yes. The county FAQ states a 10% penalty on the total tax levied for failure to list within the required period.

faqs.q: How often does Stokes County reappraise?
faqs.a: The county says it uses a four-year cycle, where state law allows up to eight years.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Stokes County property tax?
faqs.a: Use the tax search and payment portal on the county Tax Administration page, or visit 1014 Main Street, Danbury, Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm.
